findings.claim: The requireManageMembers() Javadoc references canManage() when it should reference canManageMembership(GroupModel).

verifier.reason: In services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionEvaluator.java:132-135, the requireManageMembers(GroupModel) Javadoc already references canManageMembership(GroupModel), not canManage(). Moreover, the implementation in services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissions.java:376-380 delegates to canManageMembers(group), so the Javadoc should reference canManageMembers(GroupModel) rather than canManageMembership(GroupModel).

findings.claim: GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() passes groupResource.getId() to hasPermission() and adds it to the result. That is the authorization resource ID, not the group ID (groupResource.getName()). hasPermission() resolves by name, so the per-group lookup fails, and the returned IDs do not match group IDs used in user filtering and counts.

verifier.reason: In services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:121-125, getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() passes groupResource.getId() (the generated authorization resource ID) to hasPermission() and adds it to granted, even though group resources store the group ID in resource.getName() (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:103-118) and hasPermission() looks up resources via resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId) (GroupPermissionsV2.java:141). Consequently, the per-group resource lookup fails and any returned IDs are authorization resource IDs rather than Keycloak group IDs expected by user filtering and counts in UsersResource.java:397,422,427,442.

findings.claim: Per-group resources are created without a type, because getOrCreateResource() never calls setType. As a result, findByType(server, 'Groups', ...) returns only the all-groups type resource and not the per-group resources.

verifier.reason: In server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java:120-128, getOrCreateResource() creates per-group resources via resourceStore.create(...) and updates scopes without ever calling resource.setType(resourceType), unlike init() at AdminPermissionsSchema.java:271-276 which sets type='Groups' on the all-groups resource. Consequently, resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) in services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:121 (querying r.type = :type via JPAResourceStore.java:206-229) matches only the all-groups type resource and omits all per-group resources.

findings.claim: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (no-arg) falls back to hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE). An admin with only all-groups VIEW permission therefore passes requireManage(). This lets them create top-level groups and move groups to top level in GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup, which is guarded only by requireManage().

verifier.reason: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE) at services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:70, so an admin with only all-groups VIEW permission passes GroupPermissions.requireManage() (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissions.java:279-283). Because GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup is guarded solely by auth.groups().requireManage() at services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/GroupsResource.java:180-202, a view-only admin can create top-level groups and move existing groups to the top level.

findings.claim: No migration adds the Groups type resource and the new scopes to realms whose admin-permissions client already exists, because init() returns early in that case.

verifier.reason: AdminPermissionsSchema.init() returns early when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() already exists (server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java:246-252), so the newly added Groups type resource and group scopes (lines 56, 69-71, 79) are never created for existing admin-permissions clients. No migration in DefaultMigrationManager (model/storage-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/storage/datastore/DefaultMigrationManager.java:84-126) or Liquibase backfills them, leaving pre-existing V2 realms without the Groups resource and scopes (which causes missing-scope errors and an NPE in services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:144-149).
